item.title: Staff Post - Wikiwalk Proposal
item.content:encoded:
Timer Expired. Edits made as discussed below. Author may revert at any time.

The WikiWalk team is proposing edits to this page. All proposed edits will be in a collapsible below this post, and after 7 days if there are no serious objections to the edits, the feedback received will be taken into account as the edits are made. If you have questions not directly related to the article about this project, please pm a member of the WikiWalk Team

+ Show Block
- Hide Block

It was pointed out that this article has numerous similarities with SCP-1517, namely in things that crawl replacing tissue with confectionery delights. As such, I am recommending the following edits:

Changing this:

When SCP-839 is ingested by any mammal, it will burrow through the stomach lining and towards a specialized organ. The choice of organ appears to be dependent on SCP-839's "flavour". SCP-839 will then attach itself to the organ and slowly ingest it. While the organ disappears, SCP-839 will change in form and chemical composition in order to match the organ. SCP-839 does not act as a perfect replacement, and other effects may occur. This process may take █ to ██ days to complete.

To this:

When SCP-839 is ingested by any mammal, it will burrow through the stomach lining and towards a specialized organ. The choice of organ appears to be dependent on SCP-839's "flavour". SCP-839 will then attach itself to the organ and slowly ingest it. While the organ disappears, SCP-839 will change in form and chemical composition in order to match the organ. SCP-839 does not act as a perfect replacement, and other effects may occur. This process may take █ to ██ days to complete.1

If anyone has other/better examples that could be used here please leave a comment saying so!

Footnotes
1. Similarities between the life cycles of SCP-839 and SCP-1517 has been noted. Investigation into the possibility of a shared origin is under investigation.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
As someone who's written an article that has been noted to be similar to this one, I'm probably extremely biased on this subject. However, I'll try to give as impartial viewpoint as I can.

In my opinion, it's simply something squicky that doesnt work as squick. We have candy worms, which wouldn't be bad if they were at least in some place where people might accidentally viably find them often enough that the idea of accidentally getting a real worm in your gummi worms would be distressing. Which leads to the next point; other than very small children, I can't imagine anyone really picking these things up, mistaking them for gummi worms (though I'll concede, adolescent dares do happen), and eating them. And do they have to swallow them whole? Or is it okay if the worm gets bitten and ground into pieces in the mouth? Finally, what's the point behind the organ transformation if it doesn't even do anything that drastic, really? Overall, I feel this could have been taken a lot further.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I see two different ideas here: "sugar worms that you eat accidentally thinking they're just candy" and "worms that replace your organs". They don't quite work together, and neither is explored in full.

The "worms pretending to be candy" part I just don't care about because it was done enough times already in other articles.

The "flawed artificial organs" part I can see myself liking, but at the moment it suffers from being encumbered by the other idea and not being fully explored. Why would you make something like that from sugar? Why does the subject has to eat them? Wouldn't they be damaged by chewing? Isn't there any better way of introducing them into the host's organism?

The most interesting thing that can be done with that concept is interaction of multiple wormgans within the same body, and the origin story. Both are absent here. You can do fun things with the origin story for something like this, from well-intentioned medical project, to the manufacturer intentionally sabotaging the lifespan of wormgans to create repeat customers, to someone attempting to sneakily create worm-people, to who knows what. But no of that is present in the article, and the most interesting thing that is present — brain transplant — is expunged.

Also the side effects aren't weird enough.

This article is up for review. Check it out, this needs more attention!

Ehhh…. I like the idea here, and the imagery of candy worms burrowing through your body to create candy organs really appeals to me. But this is just the minimum possible execution. It doesn't really do as much with an original idea as I'd like to see. If there could be more detail to the log at the end, even that would be enough to save it for me, but without even that detail I can't recommend this one.
